segments.title: Force K's change from sea control to sea denial
segments.body: The 1939 Force K opposed surface raiders in an economic sea-control role. In 1941 and 1942, the name referred to surface raiding forces that practised sea denial. They targeted freighters supplying North Africa. Their purpose was to make North African resupply unreliable for the Regia Marina (Italian navy) in particular, and for the Axis powers more broadly.

evidence.note: The 1939 anti-surface-raider and economic sea-control role is contrasted with the 1941 and 1942 surface raiding and sea-denial role against North African resupply, primarily by the Regia Marina and more broadly by the Axis powers. Captions render raider as radar or freighter in this passage. The caption-damaged name rager mourinho at 0:34 is read in context as Regia Marina.

segments.summary: The 1939 Force K opposed surface raiders. The 1941 and 1942 formations attacked Axis supply traffic to North Africa.

segments.title: Why Force K supplemented Malta's submarines and aircraft
segments.body: Malta's submarines and strike aircraft were already inflicting cumulative losses on Axis supply traffic. That attrition could still leave a trickle of supplies reaching North Africa. Force K's surface ships could attack an entire convoy. The aim was to destroy the convoy and stop the flow of supplies completely.

evidence.note: The transcript contrasts Malta-based attrition with a surface force stopping an entire Axis convoy pipeline.

segments.summary: In 1941-42, Force K was a surface raiding force intended to stop Axis resupply convoys to North Africa outright. Malta's submarines and aircraft were already wearing that traffic down through attrition.

segments.title: Aurora, Penelope and Force K's 1941 raiding group
segments.body: Aurora and Penelope were the two Arethusa-class light cruisers in the 1941 Force K. Two L-class destroyers completed the raiding group. The ships carried fairly heavy anti-aircraft armament between them. That armament gave the force some protection when it went out from Malta to attack convoys.

evidence.note: The transcript's caption-damaged class name is read as Arethusa, followed by Aurora, Penelope, L-class destroyers, anti-aircraft armament, and raiding in 1941.

segments.summary: The 1941 Force K paired the Arethusa-class light cruisers Aurora and Penelope with two L-class destroyers. The ships' fairly heavy anti-aircraft armament gave the raiders added security.

segments.title: Force K in 1942: strength against convoy escorts
segments.body: The 1942 Force K included four destroyers from the 14th Flotilla. Three Dido-class light cruisers completed the group. This combination could stop almost anything likely to escort a convoy. Italian battleships were the exception to that assessment.

evidence.note: The transcript describes four 14th Flotilla destroyers, three Dido-class light cruisers, and the exception of Italian battleship escort cover.

segments.summary: In 1942, four 14th Flotilla destroyers and three Dido-class light cruisers formed a force capable of stopping almost anything likely to escort a convoy. Italian battleships were the exception.
